target_customer: AI developers, vendors and enterprises deploying AI, reached through insurance brokers
problem: Companies deploying AI models lack independent assurance and insurance for model errors and AI failures. Armilla started with AI model assessment and performance warranties and moved to affirmative AI liability insurance as a Lloyd's coverholder.
business_model: Insurance MGA and coverholder earning premiums and fees, plus AI assessment and warranty products
product_category: AI risk assurance and AI liability insurance

founders.name: Karthik Ramakrishnan
founders.background_notes: YC page: VP at Element AI leading go-to-market, helped set up Deloitte's global product factory and AI offerings. YC page lists him as the only founder; the seed press release names no other co-founder. Education not found.

competitors.name: Credo AI
competitors.what: Responsible AI governance and risk platform
competitors.funding_then: $12.8M Series A announced May 2022, after the batch

technical_complexity.rationale: Model evaluation and risk assessment need ML expertise, but the larger hurdle is insurance structuring and reinsurance relationships.

defensibility.rationale: Lloyd's coverholder status and carrier and reinsurer relationships (Chaucer, Swiss Re, Greenlight Re) are slow to replicate, though insurers can write AI cover themselves.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Insurers became partners and investors rather than copying: Chaucer launched AI liability cover with Armilla in April 2025.

market_need_then: In 2022 AI governance tools were emerging, and silent AI exposure in existing policies was a later concern; demand for insurance grew with generative AI after 2023.

branding.brand_signature: AI performance warranty and affirmative AI liability coverage positioning
branding.community_and_virality: Trade press in insurance outlets covered the Chaucer product launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Name origin unknown, but the company earned insurance trade coverage in 2024 and 2025.

pivots.from: AI model assessment and performance warranty
pivots.to: Affirmative AI liability insurance as Lloyd's coverholder with Chaucer
pivots.why: Product expansion in response to demand for AI liability cover; launch dated by trade press to late April 2025

outcome_analysis: Armilla raised a $4.5M seed in early 2024 and by 2025 launched AI liability insurance with Chaucer, adding a $25M capacity expansion in January 2026. Insurer partners backed it rather than competing. It stayed small on equity funding but built a regulated distribution position as generative AI created insurance demand.
notes: One source says the seed closed December 2023; the company release is dated February 15, 2024. The January 2026 $25M item is described by Fintech Global as insurance capacity, not an equity round, so it is not recorded as a round. Village lists $1.5M total and CB Insights $6.67M over 7 rounds; these conflict. Competitor Credo AI is dated after the batch; Fiddler and others appear only in 2025 to 2026 aggregator lists and are excluded. Armilla Assurance launched Armilla Guaranteed warranty in September 2023 per the company blog. Founder education not found.
